sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: The latest official Quantitative Biology listing currently visible is labeled 26 November and was announced 27 November. The supplied 27 November signal pool and exact interval query returned no candidate papers, so five notable records from the prior available listing are provided as a relevance-ranked fallback, not a measured popularity list.
sections.claimed_contribution: The selected corpus spans computational RNA design, spatial cell-state inference, molecular binding models, and interpretable medical-image classification.
sections.unique_caveat: The five selected records predate the supplied 2026-11-25 19:00–2026-11-26 19:00 UTC window; arXiv has no official trending chart and biomedical coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
sections.abstract: KnitNet uses verifier feedback to iteratively repair candidate RNA sequences toward exact computational fold-back matches, reporting gains on five secondary-structure benchmarks and improved 3D structural self-consistency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report an average 21-percentage-point increase in exact solves versus continued sampling with 70% less time-to-solve across five secondary-structure benchmarks; they also report higher 3D self-consistency and faster inference than per-target reinforcement learning.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational folding and benchmark results only; experimental folding and biological function are not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level signal or score was available; selected for direct RNA-design relevance and quantified benchmark results, not measured popularity.

sections.title: Resolving cell states in spatial transcriptomics with SCATTER
sections.abstract: SCATTER estimates cell-type proportions and within-cell-type expression at spatial transcriptomic spots using spatial context and annotated single-cell reference profiles.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across five pseudo-spot benchmarks, the authors report higher cross-spot correlations than three comparators for 82.8–99.8% of evaluated gene–cell-type pairs, plus computational analyses of cancer and multiple-sclerosis tissue data.
sections.unique_caveat: Much quantitative comparison uses pseudo-spots; tissue applications are computational analyses and do not independently establish biological validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level HF/HN score was supplied; Semantic Scholar returned 0 citations and 0 influential citations at retrieval. Relevance-ranked, not popularity-ranked.

sections.title: Exclusion and internal structure in the association/dissociation kinetics of DNA-binding proteins in the fast diffusion limit
sections.abstract: The paper develops a coarse-grained stochastic model for DNA-binding proteins that combines footprint exclusion, diffusion, and conformational switching, and fits it to previously measured RPA–ssDNA dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive an effective Markov model and mean-field approximation for fast-diffusing proteins, then use multisegment binding states to represent facilitated exchange and the balance between affinity and remodeling.
sections.unique_caveat: The model relies on a fast-diffusion assumption and fits previously measured RPA dynamics; it is not a new binding experiment, and applicability to other proteins remains to be tested.

sections.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
sections.abstract: Deterministic equations and stochastic simulations examine how mediator dose, reaction volume, and copy-number thresholds affect reliable ternary-complex formation in a minimal binding model.
sections.claimed_contribution: In exact stochastic simulations, the author reports that small modeled volumes can fail to accumulate enough complexes despite a favorable deterministic response; volume, thresholds, completion rates, and breakup rates change modeled reliability.
sections.unique_caveat: A minimal mathematical model and catalytic extension; no experimental system or clinical outcomes are reported.

sections.title: DDxBasis: Explaining Frozen Foundation Encoder-based Medical Classification by Exact Differential Diagnosis
sections.abstract: DDxBasis represents frozen-image-encoder classifications as differential-diagnosis-style contrasts and evaluates them across five medical-image datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report exact concept-level decomposition of model decisions and performance competitive with published domain-specific methods across five datasets; they also report analyses of recovered structure and shortcut features.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective model and dataset results do not establish clinical utility or prospective performance; external-site validation remains necessary.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: The selected prior-batch papers share computational treatment of molecular constraints: verifier-guided RNA design and mathematical models of DNA binding and ternary-complex formation. SCATTER and DDxBasis each represent a single method signal in spatial omics and interpretable medical imaging, respectively.
sections.claimed_contribution: The report groups recurring methods in the selected five-paper corpus while distinguishing three-paper molecular modeling from two single-paper applications.
sections.unique_caveat: The candidate pool is empty and this small relevance-selected sample cannot establish measured popularity or a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: Follow-up work could test RNA sequence designs with structure and function assays, validate spatial-expression estimates against independent cell-type measurements, test binding models across proteins and reaction volumes, and evaluate image explanations under external-site shifts.
sections.claimed_contribution: These proposals follow from the validation boundaries described by KnitNet, SCATTER, Li and Chou, Agrawal, and DDxBasis.
sections.unique_caveat: These are research proposals based on the preprints, not clinical guidance or claims of novelty or tractability.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The latest visible listing emphasizes computational RNA design and molecular-interaction modeling, alongside one spatial-omics method and one image-explanation method. Because the supplied daily signal pool is empty and the selected records are from the prior available listing, treat this as relevance-ranked context rather than a measured arXiv trend.
sections.claimed_contribution: The main pattern in the selected corpus is explicit computational modeling of molecular constraints and biomedical prediction.
